generated_for: SACA App — symptom icon / image generation
note: Each 'label' is the exact string displayed in the app. 'image_hint' describes what the icon or illustration should depict for clarity and quick recognition by non-medical users.
removed_as_redundant: Concussion (hit to head)        → covered by 'Head injury or bump'
Chest tightness or pressure     → moved to Heart & Circulation systemic category
Burning abdominal pain          → covered by 'Upper/Lower abdominal pain'
Rectal bleeding                 → covered by 'Blood in stool or black stool'
Arm stiffness                   → covered by 'Arm pain' and 'Suspected fracture (arm)'
Limited arm movement            → covered by 'Suspected fracture (arm)' and injury entries
Low back pain (into leg)        → covered by 'Lower back pain' in body section
Limited leg or knee movement    → covered by 'Knee pain or injury'
Joint stiffness (knee or ankle) → covered by 'Ankle pain or sprain' / 'Knee pain or injury'
Nasal congestion or stuffy nose → merged into 'Runny or blocked nose'
Coughing up phlegm or mucus     → merged into 'Cough'
Difficulty breathing            → covered by 'Shortness of breath'
Feeling generally unwell        → too abstract to image, covered by other systemic symptoms
Eye redness or burning          → covered by 'Itchy or watery eyes'
Sneezing fits (hay fever)       → duplicate of 'Sneezing'
Allergic reaction               → too abstract, covered by hives/rash entries
Skin swelling or lesion         → covered by 'Hives or skin welts' and 'Skin rash'
Stomach bloating (systemic)     → already in physical as 'Stomach bloating or cramping'
Flu-like stomach illness        → too abstract to image
Irregular heartbeat             → same image as 'Racing heart or palpitations'
Increased heart rate            → same image as 'Racing heart or palpitations'
Leg swelling (systemic)         → already in physical as 'Leg or ankle swelling'
Feeling of panic or dread       → merged into 'Sudden intense fear (panic attack)'
Excessive worry or restlessness → too abstract to image meaningfully
Difficulty concentrating        → too abstract to image
Low mood or depression          → too abstract to image in clinical context
Unexplained weight gain         → too abstract for acute triage context
Memory or concentration problems→ too abstract to image
Loss of sensation               → covered by 'Numbness or tingling (body-wide)'
Sudden dizziness or shakiness   → covered by 'Dizziness or lightheadedness' (neurological)
Cold sweats                     → covered by 'Unexpected sweating' (heart section)
Sleepiness after eating         → too situational, covered by 'Excessive daytime sleepiness'
Sudden confusion after not eating → covered by 'Feeling faint after skipping meals'
Frequent need to urinate (systemic) → already in physical as 'Frequent urination'

systemic_symptoms.description: Step 1 — shown after physical symptoms. These are body-wide symptoms not tied to one body location. Grouped into 8 named disease-family categories.
